It may be discovered during inquiry; it cannot hide the desired achievement as a condition.

## The universal class

Let \(\mathfrak E_\Theta\) contain explanatory contents across the subject matters admitted by the adopted reality model and physically representable at the relevant abstraction. Let \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{adv}}_\Theta\) contain coherently posed challenges for which explanatory advance is possible in principle. Both domains are specified independently of the candidate's successes. An unfamiliar topic may not be removed solely because the candidate lacks its concepts.

Let \(U_c\) be the task of understanding and critically using content \(c\), with its use contract, and \(A_p\) the achievement task of a creative critical advance on \(p\). Define

\[
\operatorname{UU}_{\Theta,\beta}(s,\Omega)
\iff
\forall c\in\mathfrak E_\Theta\ \exists\chi,
\operatorname{Enable}(s,U_c,\chi)
\land\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi_0,U_c;\chi),
\tag{U1}
\]

and

\[
\operatorname{UC}_{\Theta,\beta}(s,\Omega)
\iff
\forall p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{adv}}_\Theta\ \exists\chi,
\operatorname{Enable}(s,A_p,\chi)
\land\operatorname{CanAdv}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi_0,p;\chi,J_p,C_I).
\tag{U2}
\]

The use tasks in (U1) concern correct reconstruction of the content's organization, not endorsement of that content as true. The achievement tasks in (U2) use the actual repair and provenance conditions. Their success must not be redefined as producing a success label. The physical grade required by each task belongs to its enabling contract. The starting family \(J_p\) and continuing-inquiry attribute \(C_I\) in (U2) are fixed by the achievement contract, not selected afterward to exclude failures. Historical novelty is required at the achievement event, not on every subsequent use of its result.

The universal explanatory class is

\[
\mathsf{UECS}
=
\{(M,s,\Omega,\beta):
M\models\operatorname{RC}(s,\Omega)
\land\operatorname{UU}_{\Theta,\beta}(s,\Omega)
\land\operatorname{UC}_{\Theta,\beta}(s,\Omega)
\}.
\tag{U3}
\]

The same \(\Omega\), boundary policy, and attribution criterion remain fixed across the quantifiers. The contents and owned tools can develop. The definition demands neither that every attempt succeed nor that every explanation be simultaneously possessed, nor that a thinker solve an impossible or incoherent demand.

The conjecture that universal explanation arrives through a qualitative jump is compatible with this class. Equality between “has once extended itself” and (U3) is not adopted as a theorem. It would require a substantive argument that rules out every remaining independently specified barrier.

# The semantic class collected

## Primitive data

An FW5 model supplies physical and historical data \(\Theta,\mathcal H\), organization structures \(D\) satisfying (O), content and occurrence domains, the representation interpretation at declared grains and boundaries, question contracts, actual control and appraisal histories, a continuity specification, and any normative relations invoked by its questions.

More explicitly, the physical module \(\Theta\) includes substrate state spaces, attribute sets, allowed process histories, controlled-action interpretations, admitted resources and disturbance contracts, and a relation of approximate realization. Let its accuracy domain \(Q_\Theta\) be a directed preorder of performance grades, with increasingly demanding grades short of perfection. The primitive physical relation

\[
\operatorname{Approx}_\Theta
(\pi,T,C,\chi;q,r)
\]

states task performance to grade \(q\) and retained ability to grade \(r\), with the operational meaning of those grades fixed by the subsidiary physical theory. It is monotone toward weaker grades. The constructor-theoretic possibility assertion is

\[
T\in\mathsf{Poss}_\Theta
\iff
\forall q,r\in Q_\Theta\ \exists\pi,C,\chi,
\operatorname{PhysicallyConstructible}_\Theta(\pi,C;\chi)
\land\operatorname{Approx}_\Theta(\pi,T,C,\chi;q,r).
\tag{CT4}
\]

The resource and side-effect class for \(T\) is held fixed in this statement. An infinitely expensive or otherwise disallowed resource is not smuggled in by the existential quantifier. Equation (CT1) is the corresponding exact ideal schema, not a claim that every physical module attains perfection.

For an owned capability at a declared grade, the protocol and constructor attribute in (CT4) must either be present in the initial organization or be reached by a **finite, owned construction history** under the same enabling contract. That history must start with presently owned processes and admitted resources, not with an unexplained constructor for the desired achievement. This fixes the meaning of \(\operatorname{Can}\) without an infinite regress of available constructors. Physical preparation here is a composition of owned physical processes. It is not defined by the later semantic authorship predicate \(\operatorname{Build}\); whether the preparation is itself a creative achievement is a separate attribution. Higher grades may require further owned construction and further declared resources.

The controlled-action and process-port interpretation fixes what physical ownership and an active process occurrence mean. The model does not recover those facts from filename ownership or timestamps. These are physical primitives, not explanatory-success primitives. Their application is a theory of the physical system. Representation is a separate semantic primitive about what its states represent. Normative interpretation, when invoked, is a separate primitive about reasons in the relevant respect. All three are exposed to criticism through represented claims; none is made true by being entered into the model.

## Defined relations and dependence order

Organization solutions and query profiles are defined by (O) and (Q). Structural accounting is defined by (E), including its functional or relational fidelity clause. Supports, contribution, interference, and preservation are defined from accounting by (S), (B), (D), and (H).

Critical bearing is accounting for the specified defect question. Reason use is a representation-preserving map into an active response suborganization. Use and standing are properties of enacted applications and appraisals. Receipts describe the provenance of arguments for claims, not their truth.

Retained and owned capability are interpreted by the protocol, invariant, and physical-accuracy constructions. Deployability and understanding apply those constructions to represented content-use tasks. Construction identifies a nontrivial binding preparation in an actual attributed history. Newness compares that result with the stated earlier repertoire. Origin is (G).

Repair is the actual, attributable change in specified obligation satisfaction in (P). Created explanatory knowledge is (EK). Recursive openness is (RC); universal understanding and inquiry are (U1) and (U2).

There is no dependency of the basic definition of accounting on origin, progress, knowledge, or universality. There is no definition of knowledge by an appraisal that already presupposes knowledge. A represented claim about a definition is an object of inquiry, not a recursive call that must terminate before the definition can be used.

## Membership

The **base class** \(\mathsf{FW5}\) consists of interpretations supplying the data above, respecting their typing, and satisfying the physical-realization and reference-coherence conditions whenever a physical attribution is made. It can describe irrational systems, false conjectures, obstructed inquiry, missing evidence, and failed attempts.

The **creative-episode class** consists of base interpretations with an actual instance of (G) connected to a critical episode. The **knowledge-creation class** consists of base interpretations with an actual instance of (EK). The **recursive-capacity class** additionally attributes (RC) to a continuing organization. The **universal class** is (U3).

An individual event need not belong to a universally capable system to be originative under (G). Universal capacity need not be demonstrated by the event. The class definitions preserve that distinction rather than treating a small creative act as a certificate of personhood, consciousness, moral standing, or universal intelligence.

# Results and discriminating constructions

## Equivariance under genuine recoding

Suppose all carriers, component relations, role bindings, maps, histories, question contracts, and attribution indices are transported along bijections preserving their structure. Then the truth of (E), (G), (P), and (EK) is preserved.

**Proof.** The bijections carry satisfying valuations to satisfying valuations in (O). Images and compositions in (F), (C), and (A) commute with those bijections. Critical contrasts and non-vacuity are preserved. The historical order, represented bindings, repertoire membership, and equivalence at the fixed grain are preserved, so construction and newness have the same witnesses. Obligation truth and its produced change are preserved. Each displayed conjunction therefore has the same truth value. ∎

The result does not apply to arbitrary compression, loss of event identity, a changed boundary, or a coarsening that identifies a relevant distinction. Those operations are not the stipulated bijections.

## A complete output description need not determine explanatory organization

Let \(P\) be a projection from full organization models to an observed input–output description, and let \(\phi\) be a fixed account-claim about a candidate and question. Suppose \(M_0\) and \(M_1\) satisfy

\[
P(M_0)=P(M_1),
\qquad M_0\models\phi,
\qquad M_1\not\models\phi.
\]

Then no function of \(P(M)\) alone agrees with the accounting predicate on both models.

**Proof.** Equal inputs to a function have equal outputs, while the required outputs differ. ∎

Parallel and priority wiring provide a concrete instance when the projection retains only endpoint values and the question concerns the active route. The same argument applies to attribution from identical emitted text and to semantic use inferred from delivery logs.

The theorem identifies missing information in a projection. It does not say that no physical or organizational evidence can ever establish the distinction, or that inventing a new mathematical notation is necessary to express it.

## A conditional bridge from argument dependence to explanatory work

Suppose an application \(u\) is an actual explanatory route for \(p\), with support \(W_u\in\mathsf S_{E,p}\). Suppose removal of \(d\in W_u\), under the stated restriction operation and the same interpretation, prevents that route from accounting for \(p\). Then \(\{d\}\) is a critical block for \(W_u\).

**Proof.** These are precisely the two membership conditions in (B). ∎

Without the explanatory-route premise, inferential essentiality does not imply explanatory work for the same question. The shadow-to-height calculation can essentially use the shadow length while doing no production work on the pole's height. The conditional bridge is useful; the unconditional identification is false.

## No promotion from record state to truth

Take two base models with identical receipt sets and appraisal events, but different interpretations of an unverified application premise. In one, the premise holds; in the other, it does not. The record states are the same and the account-claim can differ in truth.

Therefore record-state equality does not entail equality of semantic satisfaction without the relevant application premises. This is compatible with reliable checks of narrower record facts. It is not an argument that quotations, calculations, or experiments are epistemically useless.

## A nonempty finite episode interpretation

Consider a stipulated investigator whose initial represented theory contains the additive two-balances equations and an unsupported current use of \(b_B=0\). Its initial repertoire lacks the represented connection between the measurement fibre and the non-identification of mass. Its physical control organization can combine equations, represent a vector, relate a null direction to a questioned feature, and change a working use. Those prior general operations are not stipulated to contain every result they can produce.

In the episode, the investigator constructs \(v=(1,-1,-1)\), verifies \(Av=0\), and binds the nonzero mass component of \(v\) to the live identification question. It also binds \((0,-1,1)\cdot v=0\) to the offset-difference question. The response withdraws the unsupported reference use and makes the fibre explanation deployable. A counterfactual calibration row removes that particular null direction and changes the represented conclusion. A content-preserving recoding changes neither the represented dependence nor the response's use of it.

The mathematical account is the fibre construction already proved. The newly constructed binding and its actual use witness (G) at the stipulated grain and baseline. The response belongs to a critical episode. The repair obligation is possession of the limitation account and withdrawal of the unsupported identification route; the protected obligation includes retaining the original readings and the still-open mass question. These witness (P) and (EK).

A toy physical module may realize these finite symbolic operations with explicit working storage and replenished resources. Such a module is a relative consistency witness for an episode interpretation, not evidence that a scripted demonstrator, an actual language model, or a human brain has been experimentally shown to satisfy the class. The investigator's representation and control assumptions are part of the witness and are not derived from printed labels.

## Recursion does not entail universal reach

Construct a family of organizations that can represent and criticize arbitrary finite chains of methods concerning one declared domain, with return to their actual uses, but whose owned processes and all admitted extensions lack a representation route to a second independently specified domain. The recursive condition holds in the first domain; (U1) fails in the second.

This separates recursive structure from universality. Removing the barrier requires an organizational account, not merely permission to write a new topic name. Making every current rule editable also does not, on its own, establish that the missing representation route exists.

## Finite performance and universal attribution

A finite collection of successful episodes does not entail universal capacity without organizational premises. Where the model class admits both an organization continuing generally and an organization matching those episodes but stopping at an unobserved barrier, the recorded outcomes do not distinguish them.

This does not prohibit a finite **argument** about the architecture from establishing a barrier or supporting a universality conjecture. The unsupported step is from a finite outcome sample alone to an unrestricted capacity claim. A proof about an organization and a count of its successes are different evidence.

## Neither probability nor computability is secretly derived

None of (E), (G), (P), (EK), or (U3) depends on an empirical-frequency update or a merit maximization. No probability-of-truth theorem follows from the fact that a constructor or a hypothesis has worked repeatedly.

The relations can have finite or infinite interpretations and can be decidable or undecidable in particular presentations. No conclusion about their computability follows merely from being recursive, critical, explanatory, or physically represented. Conversely, a computational realization is not excluded merely because it is computational.

# Reconciliation with the supplied evolution

## What is retained

The core retained from *FW2* is explanatory realism, conjecture without prior justification, criticism as itself conjectural, fallible action, recursive scrutiny with operative return, problem recognition and values inside inquiry, substantive authorship, and universality as a modal claim rather than a large performance record. Its separation of occurrence, content, use, and truth is indispensable to this proposal. These commitments are preserved without claiming that every subsequent deduction from them was valid. [S1: Part I-A; Part II, “The model and the three standpoints,” “The recursive kernel as a relation, not a scheduler,” and “Refinement without semantic substitution”]

The executable specification contributes a useful distinction between admitting prose, enacting a working-use change, and certifying a semantic conclusion. Its implementation choices are not adopted as a definition of creativity. A rotating scheduler, JSON interface, token allowance, or storage policy is not a condition of this class. [S7: Parts I–III; S8: “Mechanical adjudication is not a neutral replacement for judgment”]

## Why the negative deductions did not finish the positive theory

The three negative notes locate a real weakness: knowledge becomes adequacy, adequacy becomes work, and work becomes an unexplained why-relation. The declaration of a primitive can be legitimate mathematics, but it cannot by itself answer the request to explain what distinguishes the relation's positive instances. Calling the final word regulative does not establish its extension. [S2: §3; S3: §3; S4: §3, PDF pages 12–14]

Several exclusions are also too strong. From “a prediction is not sufficient for an explanation” it does not follow that a prediction cannot be a constituent of an explanatory argument. From “a machine check does not certify arbitrary semantic adequacy” it does not follow that no mechanically established proposition can settle a limited semantic question under stated interpretation premises. From “a physical process is not sufficient as described” it does not follow that no further account of that very process can realize criticism. [S3: §5 B6 and §6 C8; S4: §§1–2; compare S1: “Refinement without semantic substitution”]

FW5 interprets those exclusions as distinctions between levels of claim, not as a prohibition on physical or mathematical participation. The positive burden is now carried by organization, reference, typed contrasts, and provenance. That is an added constitutive proposal, not something entailed merely by collecting exclusions.

## What the structurally extended source had already repaired

The supplied file titled *FW4* already goes beyond *FW3*. It replaces unconditional reliance on minimal supports with critical membership, gives the finite monotone theorem, recognizes infinitary joint work, distinguishes contribution from indispensability, states the correct fixed-family reach lemma, and relocates circular evidential support away from the truth of a content. Those are its improvements, not discoveries first made in this document. [S6: Parts III–IV and VIII]

Its discharge construction also separates a structural theorem, application to the target, and fidelity to the question. FW5 retains that separation. It differs by making structural accounting a proposed definition with component-level anchoring, by treating general interference without assuming monotonicity, by allowing collective contribution without singleton witnesses, and by supplying arbitrary nonlinear and constrained compatibility fibres. Its explanation proposal therefore accepts a stronger risk of counterexample than a merely sufficient discharge that can always leave the primitive untouched. [S6: Part IX; Part III.7; Part XIV]

Neither a weak local theorem nor a list of prohibitions proves that the resulting class captures every explanatory mode. That stronger claim is the constitutive conjecture stated at the beginning.

## Contribution is not necessity, and necessity is not automatically explanation

The original argument-side relation of essentiality concerns one application. It can hold in a valid reverse calculation that is not a production explanation. The FW3 proposal to identify it with membership in a unique minimal working subset is incorrect. A commitment may belong to every minimal support even when there are several supports, and an essential inferential premise need not explain the same target in the same respect. [S1: “Argument dependencies and the effect of criticizing a premise”; S5: T11]

The structurally extended source correctly makes the bridge conditional. FW5 preserves that correction and adds the distinction between a whole working block and its individual elements. It also avoids presenting the discovery of one adequate subroute as proof that an interfering full theory is adequate. [S6: R11; FW5 equations (B), (M1), and (M2)]

## More reach is not a count-based warrant

The FW3 statement that an explanation reaching more is thereby harder to vary is not a valid comparison between arbitrary contents. The valid containment result holds when the organization, interpretation, and variation family stay fixed while preservation requirements are added. It may be non-strict. The structurally extended source already states this correction. [S5: T12; S6: Part III.3]

FW5 also withdraws the special permission for a count of conjecturally independent features to order explanations for preference. A numerical division into features can change without any increase in explanatory content. Particular newly met constraints can supply reasons; their count alone does not supply those reasons. This does not prohibit mathematics about counts or numerical accounting of resources. [S5: T16; S6: R16]

## Acquisition, historical origin, and retention cannot be collapsed

The claim that every acquisition is creation is stronger than the definitions and examples support. Reacquisition by a continuing system, initial possession, transfer of a functioning organization where physically possible, and learner reconstruction require different provenance accounts. Ordinary communication can require creative reconstruction without that being a theorem about every physically possible acquisition. [S2: C2; S5: T3; S6: R3]

There is a second inconsistency in the earlier theory. Its displayed originative-act definition does not require subsequent criticism or permanent retention, but its discussion of discarding concludes that an organization cannot originate a generated content because it does not retain it as a target. The latter conclusion does not follow from that definition. FW5 keeps the useful distinction: an originative act may occur once; recursive scrutiny requires target availability when scrutiny occurs; a research record serves a further evidential purpose. [S1: “Originative acts and critical processes,” especially the displayed OCA definition and subsequent productivity paragraph; “Discarding is not criticism”]

## Actual use is not a host-maintained role label

The FW3 and structurally extended layers call deployed semantic roles record facts that a host can maintain. The executable specification itself explains why that is too strong: being shown a source is not understanding or using it. A host can record an invitation, an input, or an explicit binding. A claim about what the thinker actually used needs an interpretation of its activity. [S5: T15; S6: R15; S7: “Context is a working view, not the whole causal past”]

FW5 distinguishes these without making all observations unreliable. The bytes received can be a directly recorded event fact while their operative role remains an additional claim. Semantic target closure cannot be proved just by traversing host annotations.

## Recursion, revisable constraints, and universality

The earlier hierarchy contains useful questions but does not establish all its displayed inclusions. A definition demanding a historical extension cannot be inferred from universal capacity alone. A domain family and its member contents must also be kept in different mathematical types. FW5 separates historical extension, recursive capacity, and universality rather than inheriting the asserted inclusion. [S1: “Initial repertoire domain,” “The extensible class,” and “The universal explanatory class”]

A fixed implementation does not, merely through being fixed, exclude some explanatory domain. Its represented programs or procedures may support extension. Conversely, making every parameter editable does not supply universal explanatory competence. The assertion that a frozen language-model component necessarily blocks explanatory extensibility is therefore not established by the fact that its weights are not ordinary standing-bearing contents. An actual barrier requires an argument about the whole attributed organization under its permitted continuations. This is not a claim that any present language-model system is universal. [S1: “The organization of language models under a host” and “The learnability-universality tension”]

## Factivity, approximation, and historical indexing

A false surrounding ontology does not invalidate an accurately represented scoped dependency merely because the whole theory is false. But it does not follow that a false commitment in the very working respect explains successfully. Being tightly constrained also does not prove truth or adequacy. FW5 makes these distinctions through the explicit query, projection, and error bound rather than the phrase “factive over work” alone. [S3: §5 B4; S5: T8; S6: Part IV]

Changing the current index changes the claim being applied. It does not invalidate every proposition at the former index. The instruction in both later layers that index changes invalidate all old claims is therefore replaced by a distinction between changed applicability and a revised judgment about an earlier claim's truth. [S5: S4; S6: Part XII]

Existentially closing an indexed relation is mathematically legitimate. It yields a weaker statement that omits the witness. Requiring displayed indices is a discipline of attribution, not a theorem that existential closure is ill-formed or that a relational notion cannot also have a one-place existential projection. FW5 preserves the attribution discipline without declaring an ordinary logical operation forbidden. [S2: §3 and C1; S5: T2]

## Constructor-theoretic knowledge is not accidental longevity

The physical knowledge comparison in the notes mixes a content's adequacy, a token's survival, a current capability, and a historical creation event. Those examples do not prove extensional independence of two predicates on a common domain. The constructor-theoretic notion concerns an organized preservation capacity, not the bare duration of an inscription. [S2: C4; S5: T5; S6: Part VI; R4]

FW5 supplies a conditional common-realization bridge and retains the biological contrast. It also separates achievement at a finite physical grade from unboundedly improvable construction, and a historically unique discovery from repeatable inquiry-enabling tasks. These distinctions prevent constructor theory from being reduced either to “it happened once” or to “it must make the identical first discovery forever.”

## What the executable audit does and does not settle

The supplied audit concerns executable specification **0.2**, whereas the supplied executable specification in this packet is **0.1**. The audit also states that it did not read the semantic authority and ran nothing. Its assertions about the audited version and the DeepReason record are therefore treated as reported findings, not independently verified facts about the supplied 0.1 file or about a current repository. [S9: opening and “Residue”]

The 0.1 specification explicitly provides withdrawal of working uses and subsidiary returns. It therefore cannot be accurately summarized as prohibiting every operative elimination. The central design dispute is narrower: whether a fallible interpretation can change working use, and whether a mechanical label can stand for semantic refutation. FW5 allows the former without granting the latter infallibility. [S7: “Recursion must have an operative return” and “Withdrawal affects a use, not truth by contagion”]

The audit is right that source checks and prose-first participation are compatible. But its stated immunity of formally backed conjectures to prose-only attacks cannot be a semantic principle here. A prose criticism may expose a wrong specification, circular calibration, or mistaken interpretation of a passing execution. Checking the formal artifact does not settle those questions. [S9: §4.1; S8: “Mechanical adjudication is not a neutral replacement for judgment”]

An append-only history can be necessary for a particular retrospective research claim without being necessary for every instance of creativity. A historical evidence requirement, the memory shown to a participant, and the participant's operative memory are different requirements. Their separation is not an argument that research should discard the record it needs. [S9: §3; S7: Part III]

## What the dependency review contributes

The h-EPI review identifies why exact source-event identity and alternative support routes matter. A predecessor interpretation must not disappear from a transition claim; an independent sufficient disjunct must not inherit a defeated unused premise; an unavailable observation must not become false and then become a positive finding through negation; equal answer text must not silently substitute for an identified event with different metadata. FW5's receipt and application distinctions give those concerns a semantic expression. [S10: D1–D5]

Those are findings reported by the supplied review. This work did not inspect the current repositories, rerun their experiments, or invoke a cloud model. The supplied review explicitly says its requested DeepSeek run did not execute. The mathematical checks below concern this document's constructions, not new evidence about a model's cognition. [S10: “Execution status,” “What was checked,” and “What follows about LLMs”]

# Why a new branch of mathematics is not yet required

The recurring difficulties are largely failures to distinguish objects, indices, directions of dependence, or quantifier strengths. Sets of structured relations can distinguish redundant routes, collective infinitary support, interference, semantic roles, controlled histories, and modal capabilities. Non-computability does not require a different foundation. The present class uses existing mathematics while changing what the mathematics is asked to represent.

There is also published work expressing constructor-theoretic tasks and their implementations using sets, relations, and symmetric monoidal process theories. That supplies a concrete reason not to infer a need for new mathematical foundations merely from constructor theory's counterfactual language. That work is a formal representation of constructor-theoretic structure, not a completed theory of creativity, and FW5 does not import all its formalization choices. [R5]

The possible novelty here is a proposed **semantic organization of familiar mathematics**. Its value would be explanatory: whether it represents the distinctions that matter and supports criticisms that improve our account of creativity. Giving it a new mathematical name would not settle that issue. A genuinely new mathematical structure should be introduced when a particular necessary distinction cannot be expressed by the current one, not to make an unresolved interpretation look formally deeper.

# What could defeat this class

## A structural account that still does not explain

The most important challenge is a fully specified candidate satisfying (E), with true target anchoring, the original question preserved, substantive contrasts, and no conclusion smuggling, which nevertheless provides no explanatory account. That would refute the sufficiency claim. A genuine explanation that cannot satisfy the conditions under any interpretation preserving its actual organization would refute necessity.

Necessary mathematical truths and non-causal explanations are demanding cases. A variation that changes an axiom is a well-defined mathematical comparison, not necessarily a possible physical intervention. But the availability of some edited theory must not be used to pretend that every proof thereby answers every mathematical why-question. The declared query and the real organization of the argument remain essential.

These challenges concern the constitutive conjecture, not a missing proof of a theorem asserted to follow from set theory. The distinction matters: a definition can be exact while being a poor theory of its intended subject.

## Representation and apparent reason use

The explicit representation interpretation is not eliminated. If the fidelity and integration conditions admit a system whose apparent reasons are merely disconnected decorations, the reason-use account is too weak. If they exclude a genuine inexplicit or distributed understanding, it is too strong. No output-only test settles the matter.

The formal model must keep enough internal organization to make these criticisms specific. Merely attaching an interpretation label to a fixed response policy is not the required construction or realization. The substantive question is whether the represented distinctions actually participate in its uses and changes.

## Progress can be mis-scoped

Equation (P) is intentionally local. A dishonest choice of protected obligations can conceal severe losses. That does not make the local conjunction mathematically false; it makes an expanded claim of overall progress unsupported. The proposed knowledge-creation condition adds an adequate, newly constructed account on the actual repair route precisely to prevent unrelated novelty, mere confidence, or an endorsement from supplying the missing epistemic achievement.

A defensible case of knowledge creation that contains no such contribution would challenge (EK). A case satisfying every clause while only producing a mistaken epistemic repair would challenge the account or the bridge from it to the obligations. It must not be dismissed by inventing a favorable new grain after the fact.

## Normative content is not derived by a change of notation

The class does not derive objective aesthetic facts from non-normative data. A relation of genuine aesthetic reasons is a declared substantive input when such facts are claimed. This is a limit on the present explanation, not an excluded domain and not a concealed assertion that approved art is objectively good.

A more reductive theory must supply and defend that bridge. The present document supplies neither a proof that such reduction is impossible nor a promise that a new branch of mathematics would achieve it. It states exactly which part of an aesthetic success attribution depends on it.

## Mathematical results, applications, and the universal target

A counterexample to (M1), (M2), (I2), (O1), (T2), or the retention fixed-point result while all stated assumptions hold would expose a mathematical error. Finding that real inquiries do not satisfy those assumptions instead restricts the application; it does not refute the conditional theorem.

A physical or semantic counterexample to an application can defeat that application without changing the model-class definition. A genuine domain barrier can defeat a proposed attribution of (U3). This document does not prove that an actual person, language model, institution, or biological system belongs to the universal class. Nor does it prove the class physically empty.

No conclusion here is protected from criticism by its version label, by the availability of this document, or by its mathematical notation.

# Mathematical checking performed for this document

The displayed finite monotone identities were checked by exhaustive enumeration of all nonconstant monotone Boolean support families on two, three, and four commitments. There were respectively **4, 18, and 166** families. Critical membership equalled the union of minimal supports, and whole-set indispensability equalled their intersection, in every enumerated case. The union and intersection differed in **1, 11, and 151** cases respectively. These checks agree with the proofs; they do not establish that all explanatory support families are monotone.

Exact symbolic arithmetic checked the balances matrix's rank as **2**, its null direction as \((1,-1,-1)\), the unchanged rank after three copies of the readings, and rank **3** after adding the calibration row \((0,1,0)\). The mass and offset-difference functionals applied to the null direction returned **1** and **0**. These are facts about the stipulated matrix, not evidence that actual balances have additive offsets.

All four Boolean input assignments were checked for the parallel and priority constructions. Their endpoint outputs agree, while the active second route differs when both inputs are on. The retention operator was checked on **512** three-state successor families, including deadlocked states: it was monotone, and the union of its post-fixed sets was its greatest fixed point in every case. The accumulated-error recurrence was checked in **44** parameter-and-length cases using exact rational arithmetic. Negation preserved the empty evidence view in the four receipt-presence cases.

The infinite-support, arbitrary-fibre, relational-transport, and recoding results are supported by the arguments stated in the text, not by exhaustive testing. No proof assistant checked the whole manuscript. No experiment established the class's adequacy as a theory of human or artificial creativity. The validation boundary is mathematical construction checking, not semantic certification.

# Source register and attribution boundary

The source references below are portable locators for the supplied files and consulted public works. The proposal's definitions, repairs, and proofs are attributed to this document, not to Deutsch, Marletto, or the authors of related formal work. The original books cited inside the supplied manuscripts were not independently reread in full for this response. Their role here is mediated by those manuscripts; the public primary sources below were consulted directly.

## R1 — Deutsch on explanatory knowledge and creativity

David Deutsch, **“Creative blocks,”** *Aeon*, 3 October 2012. Relevant discussion: explanatory knowledge, conjecture and criticism, and the distinction between generating an explanation and reproducing a supplied answer. The essay is a historical primary statement, not a source for claims about the current capabilities of AI. Source: `https://aeon.co/essays/how-close-are-we-to-creating-artificial-intelligence`.

## R2 — Constructor theory

David Deutsch, **“Constructor Theory,”** *Synthese* 190, 4331–4359, 2013. DOI: `10.1007/s11229-013-0279-z`. Consulted arXiv version: `1210.7439v2`, particularly §§1.1–1.3, 3.1–3.2, and 3.8. These distinguish tasks, retained constructors, physical possibility, resources, and explanatory interpretation. Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7439`.

## R3 — Constructor theory of information

David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto, **“Constructor theory of information,”** *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 471, 20140540, 2015. DOI: `10.1098/rspa.2014.0540`. Consulted arXiv version: `1405.5563v2`, particularly §§3–6 and the restrictions discussed in §8. Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.5563`.

## R4 — Constructor theory of life and physical knowledge

Chiara Marletto, **“Constructor theory of life,”** *Journal of the Royal Society Interface* 12(104), 20141226, 2015. DOI: `10.1098/rsif.2014.1226`. Consulted arXiv version: `1407.0681v2`, particularly §§3.1–3.3, including PDF page 14 on knowledge as an abstract constructor. Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.0681`.

## R5 — Existing mathematical language for constructor theory

Stefano Gogioso, Vincent Wang-Maścianica, Muhammad Hamza Waseem, Carlo Maria Scandolo, and Bob Coecke, **“Constructor Theory as Process Theory,”** *Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science* 397, 137–151, 2023. DOI: `10.4204/EPTCS.397.9`; arXiv `2401.05364`. Relevant discussion: §§2–4 on abstract tasks, physical implementations, and composition. Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05364`.

## R6 — Structural causal organization

Joseph Y. Halpern and Judea Pearl, **“Causes and Explanations: A Structural-Model Approach, Part I: Causes,”** *The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science* 56(4), 843–887, 2005. DOI: `10.1093/bjps/axi147`; arXiv `cs/0011012`. Used for the distinction between equations, interventions, and causal organization. No particular definition of actual causation from this work is made the universal explanatory criterion. Source: `https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0011012`.

## R7 — Deutsch on objective aesthetics

Kristin Lynn Sainani, **“Q&A: David Deutsch,”** *Nature* 526, S16, 2015. DOI: `10.1038/526S16a`. A primary interview on objective beauty and the limits of our knowledge of it. It is not a completed axiomatization of aesthetic value. Source: `https://www.nature.com/articles/526S16a`.

1	# Claude Fable Semantics
2	
3	## A structural class of explanatory creativity, with selected and constructed correspondence
4	
5	---
6	
7	# Part 0 — Read this first
8	**Two words, as used here.** An **argument** is reasons why this and not that: something that can be strung together into a coherent structure to decide why this and not another. Each of its steps is of an inference form that the person using it admits (\(\operatorname{Form}_j\), Part IX), and admitting a form, like accepting a claim, is tentative; for that person, while the form stays admitted, the step rules out the case in which its premises are met and its conclusion fails. An argument rules out a claim when the claim is inconsistent with its conclusion and the claim's denial is not among its premises, in the structural sense of Part IX. An argument is never a reason *for* a claim: what it does is rule out a claim's denial, or a rival, for someone who can use it, and only while it stays usable (K2). A claim that no argument rules out is only not ruled out, and gets nothing from that; a claim whose denial an argument rules out gets nothing more than that ruling out. To **tentatively accept** a claim is a person's choice to go on with it, made for whatever reason; whatever is accepted is accepted tentatively, open to being dropped, and the semantics never defines accepting by the arguments someone holds. A premise of an argument can be a claim tentatively accepted as given, and an argument need not cite a test (Part IX). Nothing in the semantics is settled: whether a candidate meets the conditions of an account depends on the candidate, its question and its target, not on anyone's view of them, and whatever anyone accepts about it is accepted tentatively (Part VI); a theory is never settled. Where a claim taken as given is used to rule out a rival, that ruling out is a choice the person made, not something the claim does by itself.
9	## What this document claims
10	
11	An explanation is a **question-relevant organization of dependencies**, held to a target by a **transport** that is tested only by **what changes when things are changed**. The definition never asks whether a piece of the explanation "is the same kind of thing" as a piece of the world. That question has no independent content: at any level of detail, a *kind* is nothing over and above how a component responds to the changes that level admits. Two components no admitted change can separate are one kind at that level, whatever labels anyone attaches to them (Part II, Argument 1).
12	
13	Correspondence between a representation and what it represents is not an import here. It is a **relation with a provenance**. A correspondence can be *selected*, produced by variation and survival on a history of encountered changes, with no represented target in that history; or *constructed*, produced by an episode of conjecture and criticism; or merely *declared* by whoever writes the model down. The three are told apart by their histories, not their outputs, and the semantics keeps them apart (Part IV). Creativity lives in construction. Selection produces the raw material construction works on. Declaration is used only as a modelling convenience, and a claim about creativity cannot depend on it.
14	
15	Questions have provenance too. A question, meaning its target, its scope of admitted changes and what it asks, can be found as well as answered, and the semantics represents both (Part III, Argument 5). This is what separates it from any class in which questions are inputs: such a class cannot represent question-finding, and creativity includes finding questions, not only answering them.
16	
17	The **constitutive conjecture** is this: explanatory creativity is fully characterized by (i) organizations and the changes they admit, (ii) transports between organizations tested by change-fidelity alone, (iii) the provenance of those transports and of the questions they serve, and (iv) their physical realization, the instantiation and transformation of these contents in carriers (Part I). A candidate would conflict with the conjecture if an argument not using these four ruled out the claim that it is a non-explanation of its question while these four cannot represent it; so would a candidate that meets \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) on its question and contract (Part V) when such an argument rules out the claim that it is an explanation there. An argument that exhibits either rules the conjecture out for whoever can use it, while it stays usable. Part XV lists what such an argument would have to exhibit.
18	
19	## What this document does not claim
20	
21	It does not define reference in terms of uninterpreted matter. It defines reference in terms of matter **plus a selection or construction history**. Physics says what organization a lump of matter instantiates; history says how that organization came to track another. Neither alone yields representation.
22	
23	It does not say prediction is explanation. Fidelity is over **component structure under change**, not over outputs. Two systems with identical outputs and different internal routes are different organizations here, and the semantics says so (Argument 9).
24	
25	It does not supply an aesthetics independent of any declared appraisal, a probability on claims, an appraisal of its own, or a function that orders explanations or thinkers. Where a claim needs one of these, the semantics does not supply it and marks the place: a claim that invokes an appraisal or aesthetic value takes the appraisal relation as an input (Parts XI, XIV), and a claim that needs any of the others is left open (Part XIV). It does not attribute an achievement to contributors beyond what a history contains (Part XI).
26	
27	It does not decide whether any human, machine, institution or lineage belongs to the classes defined. It defines the classes.
28	
29	## What is imported, what is an index, and what is defined
30	
31	The semantics has two imports: the **physical module** \(\Theta\), which says what organization a physical occurrence instantiates at a grain, and the **appraisal relation** \(\mathcal N\), taken as an input wherever a question invokes an appraisal. Grain, boundary, continuity and the contract of admitted changes are **declared indices**: every claim is relative to them, and none is a predicate that a case meets or fails. Everything else is defined in terms of the two imports, the structural vocabulary of (O) and (Q), the declared indices and the **declared inputs**, in the order Part XIV states. No undefined predicate that says "explains" without a question and a contract, or "is a cause", is taken as an import, and no definition depends on one (Argument 6); (EX) is a defined relation of an episode, not such a predicate.
32	
33	## Grievances, anticipated
34	
35	Each answer points at the part of the document that carries it; the front matter states nothing the body does not state more exactly.
36	
37	**1. "Without declared kinds you cannot tell a cause from a correlation."** You can, and only this way. A correlation has no component that responds to an intervention on its supposed input; a cause does. That is a difference in edit-response, which is what the semantics asks about (Part II, "Kinds are edit-signatures"). A declared label adds no discriminating power: where a separating change exists, fidelity finds it; where none exists, the label asserts a distinction the level does not contain.
38	
39	**2. "So this is operationalism: a thing is what you can do to it."** A *kind* is what a level's admitted changes can distinguish. A *content* is a whole organization, which can contain components that no change at that level separates, and then they are one kind *at that level*, which is what that level contains, not a loss. At a finer level with more admitted changes they may separate. Every kind-claim is indexed to its level. That is scoping, not operationalism.
40	
41	**3. "If correspondences are selected, you have made fidelity a matter of survival."** No. Selection produces a transport. Whether that transport is faithful on changes it was never selected against turns on the transport and the target alone, not on whether it survived. Argument 3 says that a selected transport is underdetermined by its history on an unseen change wherever its population admits a differing survivor there. Survival is how the transport got there; fidelity is what it is.
42	
43	**4. "Then everything is relative to a contract of admitted changes, and nothing is independent of the modeller."** A contract is a stated subset of the changes its target admits (Part II), which are changes in whatever the target is, a garden, a mathematical structure or a melody, and not only those anyone could carry out. An account is scoped to its contract and says so. Within any contract, whether a transport is faithful at a pair turns on the transport and the target, and no assessor appears in (E). A contract that quietly excludes changes its target admits to protect an account is not caught by a rule about intentions; it is caught by the requirement that the exclusion be stated (non-vacuity, Part V), and then by any criticism that supplies the excluded change. What is independent of the modeller lies in the target and in fidelity; what the modeller chose to leave out lies in the stated scope, and so in the record.
44	
45	**5. "This is teleosemantics, structural realism or functionalism with new words."** It shares commitments with each and differs from each. From teleosemantics it takes the idea that a correspondence has a history; it differs by distinguishing selected from constructed histories and locating creativity only in the latter. From structural realism it takes structure-preservation; it differs by making preservation change-driven and component-level, and by refusing a global isomorphism requirement. From functionalism it takes substrate-independence; it differs by imposing physical realization conditions at every attribution. Whether the combination is new is a question about the literature.
46	
47	**6. "You have replaced explanation with evolution."** Selection appears at the bottom: in the arrangement Part IV describes, as one possibility and not a requirement, it produces the object layer of persistent things that explanation operates on. Construction is a separate provenance with a separate trace, and every creative attribution requires it. Nothing about construction is reduced to selection; Part IV keeps the two apart by what their histories contain, and Part XV names what an argument would have to exhibit to rule that out.
48	
49	**7. "Mathematics has no interventions."** An admitted change need not be a physical intervention. Removing a starting assumption, dropping a constraint or changing a dimension are edits on an organization, and fidelity under them is well defined. A piece of mathematics explains, relative to a question, when \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) (Part VII, D16.XV). The same goes for a melody, where changing a note or a chord is an edit, and for a philosophical claim, where dropping a premise or a distinction is one. Whether anyone could carry an edit out in a physical system bears on testing and building (Part XII), not on whether a candidate meets (F1), (F2) and (A) there, or (E) on a contract that contains it.
50	
51	**8. "Where is aesthetics?"** In Part XI, as a declared appraisal relation. Artistic effect, artistic purpose and aesthetic reasons get three distinct relations, and none is defined as another. The semantics does not decide between rival aesthetic reasons.
52	
53	**9. "'Selected' is as much a stipulation as 'is a cause'."** Selection is a physical history: a population, a variation operator, a survival condition and a sequence of events (Parts IV, XII). Whether it occurred is a claim about the physical module, fallible as any claim about it is (Part XII). A kind-label is not a claim about anything.
54	
55	**10. "Freezing the question for assessment while letting questions change across episodes is having it both ways."** It is, deliberately, and the two ways are indexed so they cannot be confused. An assessment is an event with a frozen contract. An episode is a history in which every change \(C\to C'\) carries a provenance record (D13.8). Argument 7 rules out a conflict between them, for whoever can use it.
56	
57	**11. "Kinds exist. A rule is not a cause."** A rule and a cause differ in how they respond to changes: a rule's application changes when the rule is edited and not when the world is intervened on; a cause's assignment changes under intervention. That is a difference in edit-signature (Part II), and the semantics represents it exactly. What it denies is that the difference is available before the admitted changes are fixed, or independently of them.
58	
59	## Where to attack this
60	
61	The claims the rest depends on, in the order of how much falls if they fail, are stated exactly in Part XV together with what an argument would have to exhibit to rule out each. In short: (Suff) sufficiency of \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) (D16.XV); (Nec) necessity (D16.XV); (Elim) the eliminability of kinds; (Prov) the two provenances and the underdetermination of selected transports at unseen changes where their population admits a differing survivor; (QF) the representability of question-finding. Anything else is a detail.
62

64	
65	# Part I — Commitments
66	
67	**Faithfulness without assessors.** Whether a transport is faithful on a contract is independent of whether anyone tentatively accepts it. Systems can be in error about their transports, their observations, their criticisms and their own capacities.
68	
69	**Fallibility without error-as-work.** A theory may contain a faithful scoped dependence together with errors elsewhere. What cannot count as explanation is an error in the very dependence alleged to do the work. "Explanation" in this commitment means an explanatory candidate meeting \(\operatorname{Account}(\mathcal E)\land\neg\operatorname{Dec}(t)\) on its contract (Part V, D16.XV); a theory in error offered as an answer is an explanatory candidate, which ordinary usage may still call an explanation, and whether an account is easy to vary is a separate matter (Part VI).
70	
71	**Conjecture, criticism, action.** An idea may be entertained with no argument that rules out its rivals. A criticism has a target and is itself conjectural. A thinker may act on an appraisal that no argument has decided.
72	
73	**Recursive scrutiny with operative return.** Any aspect of a system's practice, a question, a contract, a transport, a method, an attention policy, can become a target, and the result must be able to change how the system proceeds.
74	
75	**Substrate independence with physical conditions.** Any carrier may bear an organization. Every attribution of an organization to a physical system is a claim that the system instantiates it, and whether a system can is a matter of physics; here and throughout, to adopt something is to take it tentatively, open to replacement, and an attribution that the adopted physics excludes conflicts with it, as a candidate can conflict with a claim (Part VI). That an organization admits an edit is not a claim that the edit can be carried out or can come about, so an attribution does not conflict with a physics that excludes carrying out an edit the attributed organization admits (Parts II and III). Which organizations a carrier can bear, and whether what carriers of one physical medium bear can pass to carriers of another, are matters of physics as well, and substrate independence reaches as far as contents can pass between media. Where two media cannot exchange what they bear, the contents that only one of them can bear form, for a system built of the other, a barrier in the sense of Part XIII. Physical possibility enters the semantics where a content is instantiated in a carrier or transformed, as when it is held, copied, taught, tested, built or performed (Parts IV and X to XIII), and it also enters as the content of claims that a candidate can conflict with (Part VI). It does not define a question, its range of changes, an account or a conflict between candidates (Parts III, V, VI).
76	
77	**Two provenances, not one.** Selection and construction both produce correspondences. They are distinguished by their histories. Neither is reduced to the other.
78

81	# Part II — Organizations and their changes
82	
83	## Organizations
84	
85	An organization is
86	
87	\[
88	D=(V,(X_v)_{v\in V},J,B,A,L).
89	\]
90	
91	\(V\) is a set of ports, each with a nonempty value domain \(X_v\). A valuation is an element of \(X_D=\prod_v X_v\). \(J\) indexes components; each component \(j\) has a footprint \(V_j\subseteq V\). \(B\) is a set of boundary conditions. \(A\) is a set of admitted edits, closed under a partial associative composition with identity \(1\). For each \(j\), edit \(a\), and boundary \(b\), the interpretation supplies
92	
93	\[
94	L_j(a,b)\subseteq\prod_{v\in V_j}X_v .
95	\]
96	
97	The compatible valuations are
98	
99	\[
100	\operatorname{Sol}_D(a,b)=\{z\in X_D:\forall j\in J,\ z|_{V_j}\in L_j(a,b)\}. \tag{O}
101	\]
102	
103	A deleted component imposes the full relation on its ports. An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one. A changed rule is a changed component.
104	
105	Values of ports may be paths, functions, fields, mathematical structures or histories. Cyclic constraints are admitted. Several solutions remain several.
106	
107	## Roles are defined, not supplied
108	
109	No role assignment is supplied. A port \(v\) is an **input** under \(A\) when \(A\) contains an edit that sets \(v\) directly. A port is an **output** of component \(j\) when its value is determined by \(L_j\) given the other ports of \(V_j\) across \(B\). A port \(o\) is an **observation** when \(\exists a\in\operatorname{Alt}_j\setminus\operatorname{Slc}_j,\ m\in V_j\setminus\{o\}\) with \(\operatorname{asg}(m)\) defined and \(L_{\operatorname{asg}(m)}(a,\cdot)=L_{\operatorname{asg}(m)}(1,\cdot)\), where \(j=\operatorname{asg}(o)\) (D2.4, D2.6). The direction of an organization is a consequence of which edits it admits, not a stipulation about which way an equation is read.
110	
111	## Kinds are edit-signatures
112	
113	Fix an organization \(D\) and a contract \(C\subseteq A\times B\) (Part III). The **signature** of component \(j\) on \(C\) is
114	
115	\[
116	\operatorname{sig}_C(j)=\{(a,b,L_j(a,b)):(a,b)\in C\}. \tag{K}
117	\]
118	
119	Two components \(j,j'\) are **of one kind on \(C\)** when there is a bijection of their footprints under which \(\operatorname{sig}_C(j)\) and \(\operatorname{sig}_C(j')\) coincide. A kind is an equivalence class of components under this relation. For two explanatory candidates (Part V), let \(E\) and \(E'\) be their organizations and \(t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\) and \(t'=(\pi',\tau',\sigma',\lambda')\) their transports from \(D\), where \(\pi\) translates valuations, \(\tau\) translates edits, \(\sigma\) translates boundaries, and \(\lambda\) assigns each component of \(E\) a subnetwork of \(D\), its counterpart, with a port translation (Part IV). A component of \(E\) and a component of \(E'\) are of one kind on \(C\) when their signatures, read on \(C\) through \(\tau,\sigma\) and \(\tau',\sigma'\), coincide under a footprint bijection; Argument 2 uses kinds in this sense. Argument 1 makes the like comparison between an active component \(k\) of \(E\), read on \(C\) through \(\tau,\sigma\), and its counterpart \(\lambda(k)\), read on \(C\) directly with its hidden ports projected away, up to the port translation. Kinds are therefore relative to the contract; a coarser contract identifies more components, and two components of one kind on \(C\) may separate on a finer contract. A signature is built from a component's relation under each \((a,b)\in C\), not from the values its ports take in a solution; two components that differ only in those values are of one kind on \(C\), whatever the difference is called. An edit that sets a port replaces only the component that assigns the port (above), not the relations of the components that read it, and \(j\sim_C j'\) by \(\beta\) with \(\beta_*L_j(x)=L_{j'}(x)\) gives \(j\sim_{C\cup\{x\}}j'\) (FC05).
120	
121	What ordinary language calls a cause, a measurement, a rule or a constitutive status are families of signatures:
122	
123	- a **causal assignment** has a signature that changes under intervention on its output port and is invariant under observation edits;
124	- a **measurement** has a signature invariant under interventions on the measured port and variable under edits to the measuring relation;
125	- a **rule application** has a signature invariant under interventions on the world and variable under edits to the rule.
126	
127	These are functions of \((D,C)\) (D4.6, FC13), not additional data. The semantics never asks whether a component "is" a cause. It asks what its signature is. In particular, \(m\in V_j\land\operatorname{asg}(m)\notin\{j,\text{undefined}\}\land\operatorname{Changes}_C(j,A\setminus\operatorname{Slc}_j)\Rightarrow\operatorname{Meas}_C(j,m)\) (D4.6, FC4.new1). Which of the two an account offers as producing an outcome is fixed by that signature, not by the account's wording.
128
